text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a ~15m eviction burst in us-west2. Tiny GPU pods (0.25-0.5g) are getting preempted in waves, app teams reporting 503s.

ryan: Yep saw that too. Pattern looks like a taint propagation event from a drain job + scheduler trying to gang-pack and then backoff, causing a cascade.

ajay: Did we roll any scheduler weight/tuning yesterday evening?

maria: Not that I know of, but ops-bot posted a node-relabel job at 02:10 UTC. Could be correlated.

ops-bot: [alert] evictions.high(us-west2) 7765432100 — 48 evictions in 10m, median time-to-evict 12s, preempt-rate spike.

lee: Quick data point — eviction traces show many pods with affinity to /gpu-family=ampere*/ and then being rescheduled on nodes without the label, so they get rejected and requeued repeatedly. Also some kube-proxy conntrack churn.

ryan: Logs:
```
I0323 02:11:05  scheduler.go:342] preempting pod load-test-xyz due to taint:preempt=true from node/gpu-node-123
I0323 02:11:06  evictor.go:88] pod load-test-xyz evicted, reschedule attempt 1
I0323 02:11:07  binder.go:210] binding failed: node affinity mismatch: missing label gpu-family
```

ajay: If the relabel job added a taint or removed a label briefly, scheduler might preempt then fail to fit. That explains the orphaned preemptions.

maria: Impact: app SLOs degraded for ~20 minutes. Estimate ~2.4 GPU-hours wasted from churn; cost delta ~12% for the window. Need a short-term throttle and a long-term fix.

lee: Short-term mitigations I can push now:
- throttle preemptions: scheduler flag --max-preemptions-per-second=2
- extend graceful-drain-window to 90s so pods have time to rebind
- set warm-pool min replicas +2 in us-west2 to absorb tiny pods

ajay: Sounds good. Also toggle scheduler predicate that rejects nodes during relabel windows (we have a gate) — patch suggestion:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm scheduler-config --patch '{"data":{"preemptionBurst":"2","gracefulDrain":"90s"}}'
```

ryan: For medium-term: prevent taint propagation on relabel-only jobs, or make relabel jobs use a maintenance label instead of taint. Also add a post-relabel wait-check that ensures label stability before draining.

maria: I'll run the short-term changes in canary (us-west2-a) and monitor. If stable, roll to rest of region.

lee: I'll open a small runbook item for ops: include the commands and rollback steps. Also recommend adding a metric for "taint-change-rate" so we can alert before preemptions escalate.

ajay: One more thought — fractional-gang requests seem to amplify fragmentation when warm-pools are low. Can we temporarily disallow fractional-gang for tiny-gpu workloads?

ryan: We can. Patch to workload-class: "allow-fractional-gang: false" for namespace gpu-tiny, then monitor queue depth.

maria: OK running canary now. Patch will be applied at 02:22 UTC. I'll post results here.

ops-bot: [note] scheduled action: canary patch apply in us-west2-a at 7765432222 by maria.

ryan: If canary looks good, steps for stable: revert relabel job to use maintenance-label, add 2m quiesce after relabel, lower max-preemptions-per-second to 1 during relabel windows.

maria: canary: initial 10m looks stable, no eviction spikes. Will do gradual rollout. Thanks team :thumbsup:

lee: filing follow-up ticket to eng-platform backlog with proposed playbook + cost impact numbers.

ajay: ack. tagging on-call to watch next 6h window.

maria: leaving here — will update thread with post-rollout numbers.
